row.title: New Lower Bounds for Some Multicolored Ramsey Numbers
row.summary: In this article we use two different methods to find new lower bounds for some multicolored Ramsey numbers. In the first part we use the finite field method used by Greenwood and Gleason [GG] to show that $R(5,5,5) \geq 242$ and $R(6,6,6) \geq 692$. In the second part we extend Fan Chung's result in [C] to show that, $$ R(3,3,3,k_1,k_2,\dots,k_r) \geq 3 R(3,3,k_1,k_2,\dots,k_r) + R(k_1,k_2,\dots,k_r) - 3 $$ holds for any natural number $r$ and for any $k_i\geq 3$, $i=1,2,\dots r$. This general result, along with known results, imply the following nontrivial bounds: $R(3,3,3,4) \geq 91$, $R(3,3,3,5) \geq 137$, $R(3,3,3,6) \geq 165$, $R(3,3,3,7) \geq 220$, $R(3,3,3,9) \geq 336$, and $R(3,3,3,11) \geq 422$.

row.summary: Consider a finite nonnull graph G with no loops or multiple edges and no isolated points. Its Ramsey number r ( G ) r(G) is defined as the minimum number p such that every 2-coloring of the lines of the complete graph K p {K_p} must contain a monochromatic G . row.title: Combinatorial Relations and Chromatic Graphs
row.summary: Greenwood, R. E.; Gleason, A. M. Canadian Journal of Mathematics 7 (1955), 1-7. The classical paper establishing small Ramsey numbers by explicit constructions and chromatic-graph arguments: it proves R(3,3)=6 and R(3,4)=9 (i.e. every red/blue colouring of the edges of K_9 contains a red triangle or a blue K_4, while K_8 admits a colouring avoiding both), and gives the corresponding partition relations. This is the standard origin cited for R(3,4)=9. Retrieved via Crossref (DOI verified against the Canadian Journal of Mathematics record). row.summary: At present, research on Ramsey Numbers has expanded to a wider scope, not only between 2 complete graphs that are complementary to each other but also a combination of complete graphs, circle graphs, star graphs, wheel graphs, and others. That needs to be avoided in order not to get a pair of blue K_4 edges.
